title: Jupiter
about: its size, its distance from the Sun, its year and its moons. Include several specific numbers, dates or names where the topic has them, some exact and some rounded or hedged (about, nearly, more than, up to).
passages: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system. It measures about 143,000 kilometers across, roughly 11 times the width of Earth, and more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it. This GASEOUS giant is made mostly of hydrogen and helium, so there is no solid ground to stand on. Jupiter circles the Sun at an average distance of about 778 million kilometers, more than five times farther out than Earth. Sunlight needs around 43 minutes to get there. Because its path is so long, one Jupiter year lasts nearly 12 Earth years.

People around the world have watched Jupiter shine in the night sky for thousands of years. The Romans named it after the king of their gods. In ancient China, ASTRONOMERS called it the Year Star, because it crosses about one twelfth of the sky each year, matching the twelve year cycle of the Chinese calendar. In January 1610, the Italian scientist Galileo Galilei pointed a TELESCOPE at Jupiter and spotted four moons: Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto. Today scientists know of nearly 100 moons. Ganymede is the biggest moon in the solar system, even larger than the planet Mercury.
